title: Mets sending struggling starter Kodai Senga to the bullpen
content:
NEW YORK — The New York Mets are moving struggling starter Kodai Senga to the bullpen, manager Carlos Mendoza said Wednesday, after the right-hander failed to fill a gaping hole in their thin rotation adequately.

In seven starts this season, Senga owns a 10.08 ERA. Senga allowed seven earned runs, five walks and three hits while lasting just 3 2/3 innings against the Cubs on Tuesday, his second start since the Mets reinstated him from the injured list on June 16. Senga opened the season in the Mets’ rotation but carried a 9.00 ERA by the end of April, when he landed on the injured list. New York’s willingness to give him multiple starts upon a return underscores the poor state of its starting staff and depth behind it.

Senga holds minor-league options, but per his contract, the Mets would need his consent to demote him.

Senga told The Athletic on Wednesday that if the Mets were to ask him to accept a demotion, he would state his desire to remain in the major leagues.

“It’s certainly the preference,” Senga said through interpreter Hiro Fujiwara. “Going down and throwing in minor-league games probably wouldn’t be as beneficial. Pitching in a high-concentration environment like the big leagues is what brings out the good and the bad. And when the bad comes out, that’s when you can finally learn versus when you’re pitching in the minor leagues. There’s just not as much to gain from those outings.”

Given Senga’s stance, the Mets’ choices seemingly are to use him in the bullpen or let him go. Senga, however, is under contract through 2028. Ahead of the 2023 season, the Mets signed Senga, 33, to a five-year, $75 million deal. He also holds a limited no-trade clause.

Senga has never made an appearance in the major leagues as a reliever. Mendoza said the game would dictate how he would deploy Senga, leaving options open for multiple innings and back-to-back appearances.

“There’s going to be an adjustment here,” Mendoza said. “We’ll take care of him, obviously, but he’s one of those guys in the bullpen.”

Success has eluded Senga since he suffered a hamstring injury in June 2025. After finishing runner-up for National League Rookie of the Year in 2023, he pitched just one game in 2024. Before his injury in 2025, Senga’s ERA stood at 1.47. He made nine appearances upon his return and produced a 5.90 ERA. He accepted a minor-league demotion and finished the year in Triple A as the Mets slowly collapsed in large part because of a lack of quality starting pitching.

The Mets (34-44) are in a similar position in 2026. Their rotation includes just Freddy Peralta, Nolan McLean and Sean Manaea. Within that trio, Peralta has struggled, and Manaea has just recently bounced back after not being good enough to break camp in the rotation. It is likely, however, that the Mets will need to fill just one more spot because Christian Scott (hip) could return from the injured list Saturday or Sunday. Still, the Mets would need to lean on David Peterson for multiple innings for the remaining spot. Over 68 innings, Peterson has a 6.09 ERA.

The Mets are hopeful, Mendoza said, that working as a reliever simplifies Senga’s approach. In his outing Tuesday, Senga attacked with his fastball in a 1-2-3 first inning, throwing as hard as 98.9 mph, but then promptly deviated and shifted to using multiple pitches. In the second inning, he gave up five runs.

“He’s a pro, he understands where we’re at as a team,” Mendoza said. “He knows that he hasn’t been at his best. He’s been dealt with injuries and all that. He knows he is more than capable to continue to help the team to win baseball games.”
